SELECT "City" AS metropolitan_market,
       SUM("Height") AS aggregate_height
FROM "Office_locations"
JOIN (
    SELECT "id"
    FROM "Companies"
    WHERE "Sales_billion" > 200
      AND ("Profits_billion" / "Assets_billion") > 0.05
) fc ON "Office_locations"."company_id" = fc."id"
JOIN "buildings" ON "Office_locations"."building_id" = "buildings"."id"
GROUP BY "City"
ORDER BY aggregate_height DESC;

WITH building_stats AS (
    SELECT b.id,
           b.City,
           b.Height,
           PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b.City ORDER BY b.Height) AS height_percentile
    FROM buildings b
),
filtered_buildings AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM building_stats
    WHERE height_percentile >= 0.5
),
recent_offices AS (
    SELECT ol.company_id
    FROM Office_locations ol
    WHERE ol.building_id IN (SELECT id FROM filtered_buildings)
      AND ol.move_in_year >= (SELECT MAX(move_in_year) FROM Office_locations) - 2
)
SELECT DISTINCT c.name
FROM Companies c
WHERE c.id IN (SELECT company_id FROM recent_offices);
}

SELECT b."City" AS city,
       AVG(b."Height") AS average_height,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c."name") AS companies
FROM "buildings" b
LEFT JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
LEFT JOIN "Companies" c ON ol.company_id = c.id
GROUP BY b."City";

SELECT DISTINCT c.name, c."Assets_billion" AS assets
FROM "Companies" c
JOIN "Office_locations" o ON c.id = o.company_id
JOIN "buildings" b ON o.building_id = b.id
WHERE b."Height" >= 300;

SELECT c.name, c.Assets_billion
FROM Companies c
INNER JOIN Office_locations ol ON c.id = ol.company_id
INNER JOIN buildings b ON ol.building_id = b.id
WHERE b.Height >= 300
GROUP BY c.id

SELECT
    c.name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT b.id) AS supertall_buildings,
    CAST(c."Market_Value_billion" AS REAL) * 1e9 * 1.08 AS adjusted_market_value_usd
FROM "Companies" c
JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON c.id = ol.company_id
JOIN "buildings" b ON b.id = ol.building_id
WHERE b."Height" >= 300
GROUP BY c.id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT b.id) > 0;

    c.name,
    COUNT(*) AS num_supertall_buildings,
    CAST(c.Market_Value_billion AS REAL) * 1.15 * 1000000000 AS adjusted_market_value_usd
FROM "Companies" c
INNER JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON c.id = ol.company_id
INNER JOIN "buildings" b ON ol.building_id = b.id
WHERE b.Height >= 300
GROUP BY c.id

WITH supertall_buildings AS (
    SELECT * 
    FROM buildings 
    WHERE Height >= 300
),
megatall_buildings AS (
    SELECT * 
    FROM buildings 
    WHERE Height >= 600
)
SELECT 
    c.name AS tenant_name,
    b.Name AS building_name,
    CASE WHEN b.Height >= 600 THEN 'Megatall' ELSE 'Supertall' END AS building_category
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON ol.company_id = c.id
WHERE b.Height >= 300;
-- For avg stories by city, this would require separate aggregation:
-- SELECT AVG(Stories) as avg_stories FROM buildings WHERE Height >= 300 GROUP BY City;

WITH "supertall" AS (
    SELECT
        b."id",
        b."City",
        b."Stories",
        b."Height",
        c."name" AS "company_name"
    FROM "buildings" b
    JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id"
    JOIN "Companies" c ON ol."company_id" = c."id"
    WHERE b."Height" > 300
)
SELECT
    "company_name" AS "office_tenant",
    AVG("Stories") OVER (PARTITION BY "City") AS "avg_stories_by_city",
    CASE WHEN "Height" > 600 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS "is_megatall"
FROM "supertall";

votes.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT c.name AS company_name,
         b.name AS building_name,
         b."Stories" AS story_count,
         c.id AS company_id
  FROM "Companies" c
  JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON c.id = ol.company_id
  JOIN "buildings" b ON ol.building_id = b.id
  WHERE CAST(c."Market_Value_billion" AS REAL) > 400
    AND b."Stories" > 60
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT company_name,
         building_name,
         SUM(story_count) OVER (PARTITION BY company_id) AS total_stories
  FROM filtered
)
SELECT company_name, building_name
FROM aggregated
ORDER BY total_stories DESC;

SELECT c.name AS company_name, b.name AS building_name FROM Companies c JOIN Office_locations ol ON c.id = ol.company_id JOIN buildings b ON ol.building_id = b.id WHERE CAST(c."Market_Value_billion" AS REAL) > 400 AND b."Stories" > 60 ORDER BY SUM(b."Stories") OVER (PARTITION BY c.id) DESC, c.name, b.name

WITH "comp_filter" AS (
  SELECT "id", "name"
  FROM "Companies"
  WHERE CAST("Market_Value_billion" AS REAL) > 400
),
"buildings_filter" AS (
  SELECT ol."company_id", b."name" AS "building_name", b."Stories"
  FROM "Office_locations" ol
  JOIN "Buildings" b ON ol."building_id" = b."id"
  WHERE b."Stories" > 60
)
SELECT cf."name" AS "company_name", bf."building_name"
FROM "comp_filter" cf
JOIN "buildings_filter" bf ON cf."id" = bf."company_id"
JOIN (
  SELECT "company_id", SUM("Stories") AS "total_stories"
  FROM "buildings_filter"
  GROUP BY "company_id"
) agg ON cf."id" = agg."company_id"
ORDER BY agg."total_stories" DESC;

       JOIN "Companies" c ON c."id" = ol."company_id"
       WHERE b."Height" > 300

              ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c."Industry" ORDER BY c."Sales_billion") AS rn,
              COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c."Industry") AS cnt
       FROM "Companies" c

       SELECT "Industry", AVG("Sales_billion") AS median_sales

       GROUP BY "Industry"
